subject: Workload velocity discovery — action grid & sizing ask
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@fastcart.com>, Rachel Liu <rachel.liu@fastcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Workload velocity discovery — action grid & sizing ask

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick written recap and proposed action grid so we can move to a draft sizing estimate. High level takeaways (please correct if I misunderstood):

- Primary integration: FastCart checkout assistant (server-side API).
- Peak behavior: ~220 QPS for short bursts (expected ~5-8 minute bursts, 3–4 times per day).
- Sustained baseline: 18–30 QPS steady during business hours.
- Tokens per request: median ~140 tokens; peak up to ~700 tokens for long receipts (OCR + context).
- Streaming: Approximately 40 concurrent streaming sessions during peak bursts (audio->text continuation + partial responses).
- Latency target: FastCart would like 95th percentile end-to-end response < 400 ms for non-streaming and first-token for streaming < 300 ms.

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed):
1) Sam/Rachel: Share the sanitized workload-sample.csv you mentioned (request-level rows: timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, streaming_flag). I attached a simple template (workload-sample.csv) — please paste or export there.
2) Marissa: Can you take the sample and run a quick tokens/sec and QPS sketch? I think we should return an initial compute estimate that shows both: a) steady-state cost/throughput and b) burst capacity required (minutes-long).
3) Neha: Note any customer constraints (data residency, retention) — Sam flagged EU data for a subset of customers; we should call that out.
4) Diego: I'll produce a short sizing note with the raw math (tokens/sec peak, expected batching impact, preferred concurrency settings) and propose a breakout call next week to review.

Attachments: workload-sample.csv (template), redwood-sizing-cheatsheet.pdf (short reference).

Thanks — Diego

--

Subject: Re: Workload velocity discovery — action grid & sizing ask

Thanks Diego — we've got the asks. A couple quick clarifications before I run the sketch:

- When you say "peak up to ~700 tokens," is that tokens_out (model-generated) or total (in+out)? That matters for batching math.
- For streaming sessions, are those interactive user sessions (one session = one persistent stream) or per-request short streams? If the former, concurrency budget is tied to active users rather than QPS.

Initial quick sketch (back-of-envelope):
- If peak is 220 QPS and worst-case tokens = 700 tokens_out per request -> peak token throughput = 220 * 700 = 154,000 tokens/sec.
- With average tokens 140 (in+out combined), steady-state ~ 18–30 QPS -> ~2,520–4,200 tokens/sec.
- For streaming: 40 concurrent streams, assume average token emission rate 10 tokens/sec -> ~400 tokens/sec additional load during peak streaming window.

Implications:
- Batch sizing: At high QPS/long sequences, continuous batching will be critical to avoid per-request kernel overhead.
- Memory/KV cache: Long requests (700 tokens) increase KV cache pressure and may require larger instance types to avoid eviction.
- Fallback policy: Recommend a canary model with shorter-context variant for extreme bursts to keep latency SLOs.

I'll put together a 1-page estimate (GPU type options, estimated concurrency per GPU, and cost ballpark) after Sam sends the CSV sample.

- Marissa

Diego / Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications and I dropped the sanitized sample in the Drive link below.

Clarifications:
- The 700 tokens number is model-generated tokens_out for long receipts (OCR + full itemization). Typical request total is in+out ≈ 850 tokens in the worst case.
- Streaming sessions are interactive user sessions (persistent streams) — one active user corresponds to one concurrent stream. Short requests are also used (~5–10 tokens) for quick suggestions.
- Data residency: EU subset applies only to orders placed from EU customers; those requests will be routed through our EU region.

Quick ask: can you include an estimate for first-token latency and sustainable throughput (QPS per GPU) given batching disabled vs enabled? We need to understand whether we should provision Dedicated capacity or rely on Hosted with capacity fallback.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-workload-sample

- Peak token/sec calc (separate columns for tokens_out-only and total in+out)
- Estimated QPS per GPU (small/medium/large inference instance families) with batching on vs off
